clue.text: Put in an awkward position — it's what Trump's good at

definitions.meaning: to leave someone stuck with no good move, as when a ball is blocked from a clear shot
Judd Trump is a world champion player of the cue game played on a large green-baize table

explanation.surface: A jibe at a politician whose real talent is cornering his opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump is not the US president but Judd Trump, an English champion at the cue sport.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to trap someone in a difficult spot; as a noun it names the game Judd Trump plays.

clue.text: 'Sign on sheet!' — force individuals to stand around

indicators.note: surrounding, so the individuals enclose the force
in a down clue standing upright reads from the bottom, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: individuals are single ones
G is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: An order to sign a sheet, then a demand to force people to their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In printed music, the segno is a symbol marking where a repeat begins.

clue.text: Real SOS at sea, when unable to propel boat?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A genuine distress call from sailors who cannot row their boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Without oars, a rowing boat has no means of moving through the water.

clue.text: Hunk leaving northern English port

indicators.note: going out of, so a letter departs from the lump

parts.note: a knob is a lump or hunk, as of butter

explanation.surface: A handsome man leaving a seaport in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northern English port' looks like one phrase but splits: northern and English are wordplay, port alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kobe is a major Japanese seaport near Osaka.

clue.text: Laura's selective about who may introduce them

indicators.note: about can mean around in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Laura is choosy about whom she will introduce to her friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar: words like who, which and that begin a subordinate clause describing a noun.

clue.text: Member of Parliament enthralled by that woman's big boobs

indicators.note: held captive by, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: belonging to that woman is hers
a group of owls is called a parliament, so one member of it is an owl

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style tale of an MP captivated by a woman's figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The MP is a bird: a parliament is the collective noun for owls.
explanation.definitionFit: Boobs here are blunders, and big ones are glaring mistakes, the classic schoolboy kind.

clue.text: Pimp's beginning to exploit her virtue — however, he may not succeed

indicators.note: read as 'how ever', any old way, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: the beginning of the word exploit, its first letter, followed by the words her virtue as written

explanation.surface: A seedy story of a pimp starting to take advantage of a woman's chastity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'however' (any old way) signals the anagram of PIMPS, E and HER VIRTUE, where E is the beginning of 'exploit'; it reads as a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This person is next in line to a title only until a nearer relative is born, so the inheritance is not certain.

clue.text: Potential fly-by-night's below royal rank

indicators.note: rank means foul or dreadful, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A shady character ranked below royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The fly-by-night is a moth, a creature flying at night, and the answer is the hairy caterpillar of the tiger moth.
explanation.definitionFit: This furry caterpillar will grow into a tiger moth, an insect that flies after dark.

clue.text: Shocking treatment in part upset old prince

indicators.note: the treatment's letters go inside the part
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a role is an actor's part
ECT, electroconvulsive therapy, is a treatment using electric shocks

explanation.surface: An old prince upset by some appalling treatment of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Electors were German princes entitled to choose the Holy Roman Emperor.

clue.text: Note sea's rising — go in wearing these

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: so (or sol) is a note in sol-fa
the deep is the sea

explanation.surface: Swimmers advised to wear the right kit as the tide comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedos are a brand of tight swimming trunks, worn for going into the water.

clue.text: Republican (American) rude, Joe admits

indicators.note: lets in, so the soldier's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: GI Joe is an American soldier
ribald means coarsely or crudely humorous

explanation.surface: A crude remark from Joe, a Republican, recorded with a note that he is American.
explanation.walkthrough: The Republican is not a US politician but the Italian patriot who fought for a united republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi was a leading nineteenth-century Italian republican and revolutionary.

clue.text: One's often in meadow making love — it's wrong to look

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
a cross marks a wrong answer
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A couple caught making love in a meadow, and a warning that it is rude to stare.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy is a wild flower commonly growing in grassland and meadows.

clue.text: Extremely short after nothing's done

indicators.note: the cut-down word follows the zero

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: short means missing its final letter

parts.note: extremely means very

explanation.surface: A complaint that something ended almost at once, once nothing was left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finished is over, as when a match or party is at an end.

clue.text: Specified details put in order

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An instruction that the particulars be arranged as laid down.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean laid down explicitly, as terms in a contract are set out.

clue.text: Underwear that's uncool for fashion leaders? It's not important

parts.note: smalls is British slang for underwear

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A sneer at underwear too dowdy for the trendsetters, followed by a shrug.
explanation.definitionFit: Small stuff is trivia, minor matters not worth worrying over.

clue.text: Writer Virginia, receiving honour, is coming back

indicators.note: returning, so the whole assembly is read backwards
taking in, so the state abbreviation holds the other letters

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A writer from Virginia returns home after being honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns the whole of VOMISA round.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific science-fiction author, known for the robot stories.

clue.text: Boards with yours truly over boozer (King's Head in Salisbury)

indicators.note: in an across clue, over means turned back to front

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
a boozer is British slang for a pub, also called a bar
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone heading for a pub called the King's Head in Salisbury, an English cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Head is a common British pub name, but here it is split: K for king, then the head of Salisbury.
explanation.definitionFit: To board a ship or plane is to get on it, to go aboard.

clue.text: Public transport cut — complaint of the countryside

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a bus is public transport
colic is an ailment, a complaint of the stomach

explanation.surface: Rural folk grumbling that their bus service has been axed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic means rural or pastoral, relating to country life.

clue.text: Swine has large following in capital

indicators.note: these letters go inside the beast

parts.note: a swine is a beast, a nasty person
F is short for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A nasty character with a big following in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfast is the capital city of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Corrie's sacked staff

indicators.note: sacked can mean ransacked, wrecked, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Coronation Street, a British TV soap nicknamed Corrie, has fired its employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosier is a bishop's hooked pastoral staff.

clue.text: Single nurses are far from impressed

indicators.note: holds as a nurse holds a baby, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: single means unmarried
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Unmarried nurses are unimpressed, perhaps by their suitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Unawed means not filled with awe, hence not impressed in the slightest.

clue.text: Country screwed from the start with someone like Boris briefly around

indicators.note: surrounding the other letter
cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Boris Johnson went to Eton, the English public school, so he is an Etonian

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A country screwed over from day one by a Boris-type figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country in northern Europe.

clue.text: Hurry down to feed plant — can start in kitchen first

indicators.note: says the toilet and the kitchen letter come before the rest

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, a loo

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
feeding something puts it inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a plant is a spy placed inside an organisation
nap is the soft down or pile on fabric

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions for watering a plant from a can.
explanation.walkthrough: The can is the toilet and the plant a spy; nap is fluff on cloth, like down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom look snappy is an order to be quick, to hurry up.

clue.text: Go back in cab at seven

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Arranging to come home by taxi at seven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go at something is having a try, an attempt, a shot at it.

clue.text: Rubbish government consumed by nastiness

indicators.note: eaten up by, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: bile is bitterness, nastiness

explanation.surface: A complaint that government is rubbish, eaten up by spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is nonsense, worthless talk, from the dirty water in a ship's hull.

clue.text: Gave excellent service to Ant at first, upsetting partner

indicators.note: at first means take the first letter
in a down clue upsetting turns letters upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Dec is the TV partner of Ant in the British presenting duo Ant and Dec

explanation.surface: A waiter serving Ant brilliantly, upsetting the partner who was left waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a famous British TV presenting double act.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, to serve an unreturnable ball is to score a winning serve.

clue.text: I'm off distributing aid to Brussels

indicators.note: dealing out, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union, EU

explanation.surface: An aid worker leaving after handing out supplies to Brussels.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, a parting remark meaning one is leaving.

clue.text: Quick look round in Hollywood location recalled a feature of Manchester

indicators.note: going round, so the glance's letters wrap the other piece

parts.note: a scan is a quick look over something
in means fashionable, as is hip

indicators.note: called back, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: Hollywood is in LA, Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Someone glancing around Hollywood and remembering a landmark from Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manchester Ship Canal links the city to the sea, a famous waterway of the city.

clue.text: One's Queen having arguments about taxes

indicators.note: around, so the quarrels enclose the other letters

parts.note: tiffs are petty quarrels
one is A, as in a single item
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A queen bickering with her ministers over taxation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tariffs are duties charged on imports, a kind of tax.

clue.text: Point at Lord Hall gatecrashing celebrity finale

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: barging in uninvited, so these letters go inside the others

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity
Lord (Tony) Hall was Director-General of the BBC, abbreviated DG

explanation.surface: A peer crashing a celebrity party just as it ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Hall, Lord Hall, ran the BBC as its Director-General, the DG.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the last stage of a chess game or any process, its finale.
